### Functions!

Redoes a bunch of stuff that you do lots (avoids copy/paste!)


```{r}

# rnorm generates a number of random numbers:

df <- tibble(
  a = rnorm(10),
  b = rnorm(10),
  c = rnorm(10),
  d = rnorm(10)
)

head(df)

```


If I wanted to manually rescale:

```{r}

df <- df |> 
  mutate(a = (a - min(a, na.rm = TRUE)) / (max(a, na.rm = TRUE) - min(a, na.rm = TRUE)))

head(df)

```


If you wanted to do this for a, b, c, and d, you'd copy/paste it a bunch. But errors may arise!!!

So: functions!

```{r}

# set a function

rescale01 <- function(x) {
  value <- (x - min(x, na.rm = TRUE)) / (max(x, na.rm = TRUE) - min(x, na.rm = TRUE))
  return(value)
}

# now use the function!

df |>
  mutate(
    a = rescale01(a),
    b = rescale01(b),
    c = rescale01(c),
    d = rescale01(d)
  )


```


OR you can use the everything() function with your new function!

```{r}

df |>
  mutate(across(everything(), rescale01))

```

Functions must have a name that is 1. easy to remember, 2. easy to spell, 3. describe the function

Functions have arguments, function(x) has one argument, function(x,y,z) has three.

Function body is contained within the {  } blocks containing code

Return statement is what the function returns


### Functions minimize repetitive tasks!

Example 1: convert Fahrenheight to Celsius

```{r}

# simple function:

temp_C <- (temp_F - 32) * 5 / 9

```

Let's make the function

```{r}

f_to_celsius <- function() {
  # code goes here!!!
  
}

```


```{r}

# make sure to comment the function as well!

# assign an argument in function(temp_F), temp_F is the argument!!

f_to_celsius <- function(temp_F) {
  # convert temp_F to C
  temp_C <- (temp_F - 32) * 5 / 9
  # write what it will return
  return(temp_C)
}


f_to_celsius(32)  # will give 32 farenheight to celsius (which is zero!)


```



```{r}

c_to_kelv <- function(temp_c) {
  #convert celsius to kelvin
  temp_K <- temp_c + 273.15
  # return
  return(temp_K)
}


c_to_kelv(2)


c_to_kelv(f_to_celsius(32))

```

OK what if you want to make a function for a plot?

You can make your own personalized theme, or exactly the same parameters



```{r}



pal <- pnw_palette("Lake", 3, type = "discrete")

ggplot(penguins, aes(x = body_mass_g, 
                     y = bill_length_mm, 
                     color = island)) +
  geom_point() +
  geom_smooth(method = "lm") +
  scale_color_manual("Island", 
                     values = pal) +
  theme_bw()


```

Let's make this into a function:


```{r}


# if you add data = penguins in the function() area, this would set a default!!!
penguinplot <- function(data = penguins, x, y) {
  pal <- pnw_palette("Lake", 3, type = "discrete")

  ggplot(data, aes(x = {{x}}, y = {{y}}, color = island)) +
    geom_point() +
    geom_smooth(method = "lm") +
    scale_color_manual("Island", values = pal) +
    theme_bw()
}


```

WHENEVER you have a function being called from within a dataframe, you need to add a curly-curly {{}}!!!

```{r}

# if you have the dataframe preset, no need to specify penguins
penguinplot(penguins, x = body_mass_g, y = bill_length_mm)


penguinplot(penguins, x = body_mass_g, y = flipper_length_mm)

```

```{r}

penguinplot(x = body_mass_g, y = flipper_length_mm)+
  labs(title = "Testing functions!")

```

###Adding control flow with if-else:

Let's say we want the user to be able to choose their own path

```{r}

a <- 4
b <- 5

# The parenthesis has to include a logical statement.

if (a > b) {
  f <- 20
} else {
  f <- 10
}

f

```

Now let's add it to our plot!

```{r}

myplot <- function(data = penguins, x, y, lines = TRUE) { # you must add an argument for lines
  pal <- pnw_palette("Lake", 3, type = "discrete")
  
  if (lines == TRUE) {  # IF lines is exactly equal to true, do the following:
    ggplot(data, aes(x = {{x}}, y = {{y}}, color = island)) +
      geom_point() +
      geom_smooth(method = "lm") +
      scale_color_manual("Island", values = pal) +
      theme_bw()
  } else {              # IF lines is not TRUE, no geom smooth:
    ggplot(data, aes(x = {{x}}, y = {{y}}, color = island)) +
      geom_point() +
      scale_color_manual("Island", values = pal) +
      theme_bw()
  }
}

myplot(x = body_mass_g, y = flipper_length_mm, lines = FALSE)

```
